transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in New York City, I'm Dwahili Saikoutau.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says President Trump is still an ally, but he warns
in an interview on NBC's Meet the Press that formally siding with Russia's leader Vladimir
Putin would be an historic mistake.
I don't want to live in illusions, but I think that we have to be pragmatic.
If the United States will take, officially, will take the side of Russia, of course, if
these two countries will be together, of course, of course we will not prevail, and we will
not be able to stand.
It's understandable.
That's why we hope that the president, his team, will be on our side minimum in the middle.
During the interview, he suggested the U.S. government may have been responsible for an
interruption to his country's use of the Starlink satellite, which helps support military intelligence
and save lives as Russia continues its strikes against Ukraine.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney confirms that four service members were killed and
dozens were wounded during a fire at a military base in Alberta.
From Toronto, Dan Karpenchuk reports.
Military officials say the fire broke out at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright late Saturday
afternoon and rapidly spread through the base.
Carney says what followed was one of the worst tragedies for the Canadian military in peacetime.
Carney says next of kin have been notified and dozens of more seriously wounded personnel
have been taken to local and regional hospitals.
He says the soldiers training at the base are from the Princess Patricia's Canadian Light
Infantry, one of Canada's main frontline regiments.
They come from communities across the country and include members of the reserves and regular
force.
They said, quote, those we lost and were injured were training to defend Canada, now Canada
serves them.
Flags at provincial and federal buildings will be lowered.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpenchuk in Toronto.
High fuel prices continue to stretch family budgets as people prepare for holiday shopping
and travel.
GasBuddy estimates Americans have spent about $82 billion more on gasoline since March 1st
compared to the same period last year, NPR's Windsor Johnston reports.
Petroleum analyst Patrick Dahan says at this point the pressure has extended beyond the
gas pump.
He says diesel costs are working their way through the supply chain.
I would like to say that the U.S. economy, the engine, is powered by diesel.
Dahan says heavy, bulky goods and perishable foods are especially exposed, including turkeys
heading to grocery stores for Thanksgiving.
Holiday travelers also face higher fuel costs, whether they drive or fly.
There's no way to book now and beat it.
You can't avoid the increase in fuel when what comes out of a barrel is fueling the
entire U.S. economy.
He says relief depends on what happens next in the conflicts overseas that continue to
disrupt oil supplies.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
It's NPR.
Officials from Congo say the Ebola outbreak has spread to an eighth province.
This comes as Kenya has announced four new infections.
As Michael Koloki reports, this brings the total number of confirmed cases in the East
African nation to at least seven.
In a statement yesterday, Kenyan authorities said that all four patients were already in
quarantine when they developed symptoms, adding that tests confirmed they have the Bundibogia
strain of Ebola.
The statement noted that one of the four is a close male relative of the first Ebola patient
in the country, who passed away earlier this month after traveling from the Democratic
Republic of Congo to Kenya through Uganda.
Health officials said that the additional three new cases are health workers who had
attended to the first Ebola patient, with authorities noting that the three are receiving
supportive care at a designated facility.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Koloki in Nairobi.
French authorities say 2,300 people were arrested after violence broke out during mass student-led
demonstrations across the country yesterday.
Researchers said some 800,000 people participated in the acting government rallies, while local
officials estimated the crowd to be around 550,000.
A televised address to the nation, President Emmanuel Macron, blamed insurrectionist elements
from "radical far-left groups" for what he called "unrestrained violence."
A 19th-century town hall in central France was nearly destroyed due to a fire that caused
the roof to collapse.
I'm Dua Lisa Calteau in "PR News" in New York City.

topics.text: Zelensky warns NBC that a U.S. alliance with Putin's Russia would be a historic mistake
Fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta kills four soldiers and wounds dozens
Gasoline and diesel costs push holiday travel and turkey prices higher as Americans spend billions more
Ebola outbreak spreads to an eighth province in Congo as Kenya reports four new infections
Over 2,300 arrested as mass student protests in France turn violent; Macron blames far-left groups
Fire in a 19th-century central French town hall causes roof to collapse
